target.title: fix(agent): exit nonzero when gateway runs do not complete
target.body:
Fixes #110946

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running an agent through the gateway, especially with `openclaw agent --json`, could receive a successful `ok` / `completed` result and process exit code 0 after the explicit run deadline had already aborted a nonterminal `toolUse` result.

This made unattended shell and CI automation treat an incomplete agent run as successful. Gateway responses that were already classified as `timeout`, `error`, or `cancelled` could also be emitted while the CLI still exited successfully.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolved gateway runs now use the actual `AbortSignal` as the source of truth when projecting an aborted nonterminal result. The signal reason is preserved as `timeout`, `rpc`, or `restart`; elapsed duration alone is deliberately not used, so slow but non-aborted runs are not reclassified.

The CLI now marks `timeout`, `error`, and `cancelled` gateway responses with `process.exitCode = 1` only after writing text or JSON output. This lets stdout drain completely while preserving the existing native exit codes for local SIGINT and SIGTERM handling. A final `stop` result remains successful even when timeout cleanup has already aborted the controller.

## User Impact

Shell scripts and CI jobs can trust both the gateway terminal envelope and the CLI exit status: incomplete or failed agent runs return nonzero, while valid long-running completions and cleanup races remain successful.

There is no wire-format change and no behavior change for successful or in-flight runs.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the issue regression produced a top-level `status: "ok"`, `summary: "completed"`, `stopReason: "toolUse"`, and `livenessState: "working"` after a timeout abort.

### Live gateway behavior

I started the branch gateway from the tested patch as a real loopback gateway on a separate port with an isolated temporary config, state directory, workspace, and session keys. The run used the plugin-owned Codex app-server runtime with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`; the existing local gateway was not stopped or modified. The same tested patch is now rebased at `0a89793e`.

Successful terminal control (`stop`):

```text
$ openclaw agent ... --message "Reply exactly LIVE_SUCCESS and do not use tools." --timeout 30 --json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "payload": "LIVE_SUCCESS",
  "stopReason": "stop"
}
exit=0
```

Timeout case: the prompt immediately invoked `exec_command` with `sleep 20`, while the CLI deadline was 5 seconds. The gateway log confirmed that the Codex app-server turn timed out waiting for progress and retired the timed-out client.

```text
$ openclaw agent ... --message "<redacted timeout prompt>" --timeout 5 --json
{
  "status": "timeout",
  "summary": "aborted",
  "payload": "Request timed out before a response was generated. Please try again, or increase `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` in your config."
}
exit=1
```

This is after-fix runtime evidence from the branch gateway and CLI, not a fixture-backed mock. The temporary gateway shut down cleanly after both controls.

Validated on Node 24.15.0 against current `main`:

- `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` — 251 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts src/commands/agent.test.ts` — 125 passed, 1 pre-existing skip.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root` — passed.
- Focused `oxfmt --check` and type-aware `oxlint` for all four changed files — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed, including CLI bootstrap checks, plugin SDK export checks, Control UI build, and performance budgets.
- Repository autoreview — clean, no actionable findings.

The regression coverage includes the reported timeout case plus negative controls for a long run without an abort signal, a run before its deadline, disabled timeouts, and a final assistant response after timeout cleanup.

AI-assisted: yes, with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and tests and understand the changes.
